chunks: And whoever among you cannot find [the means] to marry free believing women, then [marry from] what your right hands possess, i.e., your believing slave girls. And Allah is most knowing of your faith. You are of one another. So marry them with the permission of their people and give them their dowry in kindness. [They are] chaste, neither of those who commit unlawful sex randomly nor those who take secret lovers. But when they are married, if they commit adultery, for them is half of the punishment for free [unmarried] women. [This is] for whoever among you fears sin. And that you remain chaste is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

key_terms.نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى الْمُحْصَنَاتِ: Half the punishment of free women

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for marrying believing slave girls if one cannot afford free women?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this verse (Ayat al-Nikah) is central to the permissibility of temporary marriage (Mut'ah), as the phrase 'with their owners' is interpreted by scholars like Al-Tabarsi to imply a fixed duration rather than permanent ownership. It establishes that slave girls must be chaste and their marriage requires the consent of their masters, with a reduced penalty for adultery reflecting their social status. The verse concludes by encouraging patience in securing a permanent marriage as superior to this alternative to prevent sexual sin.
